stories.title: Bermuda Championship Final Round — Smotherman and Power Chase the Title at 16-Under
stories.angle: Smotherman and Power share the 54-hole lead at 16-under entering the final round at Port Royal Golf Course; tee times moved up due to 35mph winds; $1.08 million winner's purse and FedEx Cup Fall points on the line

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Final round today at Port Royal.

Smotherman and Power are tied at 16-under. 12 players within 4 shots. Wind forecast: 35mph.

The Bermuda Championship winner gets decided this morning. #PGATour

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Final round is underway in Bermuda.

Smotherman is going for his second PGA Tour win this month. Power needs this for his FedEx Cup season.

Every shot counts. #PGATour #BermudaChampionship

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

The 2026 Butterfield Bermuda Championship comes down to Sunday at Port Royal.

Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power are tied at the top, both at 16-under 197 after three rounds. They share the lead heading into a final round that's set to be played in challenging conditions — winds up to 35mph are forecast, which is why officials moved tee times up and sent players out in three-ball groupings to beat the worst of the weather.

Two shots back, there's a chasing pack that could make things very interesting. Taylor Moore, Corey Conners, and Ben Silverman are all at 14-under. Twelve players in total are within four shots of the leaders — plenty of firepower left in the field.

The winner earns $1.08 million and a crucial chunk of FedEx Cup Fall points. Follow along today for updates.

article.headline: Bermuda Championship Final Round Preview: Smotherman and Power at 16-Under, Chasing Pack Ready

stories.title: LIV Golf 2.0 Verdict: DeChambeau Commits, Rahm Exits as Sunday Deadline Passes
stories.angle: Jon Rahm formally exited LIV, PGA Tour future unsettled; DeChambeau commits to LIV 2.0 as reportedly committed; bankruptcy court must still give final approval Nov 5

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
The LIV Golf 2.0 roster deadline has passed.

Jon Rahm is out. Bryson DeChambeau is reportedly in, committed to the restructured league.

The Nov. 5 bankruptcy hearing is now the next big date. Golf's civil war continues.

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Jon Rahm left LIV Golf. His PGA Tour future is still unsettled.

Three consecutive individual LIV season titles. Three years of golf outside the traditional tour.

What's next for Rahm is now one of golf's biggest open questions.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Golf's most complicated storyline took another turn over the weekend as the LIV Golf 2.0 player commitment deadline came and went.

Jon Rahm, who won three consecutive individual LIV season titles, has formally departed the league and finalized a separation agreement. His PGA Tour future remains unclear after three years playing outside traditional golf's top circuit. Rahm's next step will be one of golf's most-watched off-course developments in the months ahead.

Bryson DeChambeau is reportedly staying. According to sources cited by ESPN, DeChambeau remains committed to LIV 2.0 and has been working behind the scenes to support the league's restructuring. His original contract was rejected by a bankruptcy court along with those of 18 other players, effectively making him a free agent — but he appears to be choosing to remain within the LIV orbit.

The real deadline may be November 5, when a U.S. bankruptcy judge holds a final hearing on the restructuring deal. Until then, the future of the tour that reshaped professional golf remains officially unresolved.

article.headline: LIV Golf 2.0 Deadline Day: DeChambeau Reportedly Commits, Rahm Formally Exits

stories.title: Power's FedEx Cup Stakes — A Win in Bermuda Transforms His Season
stories.angle: Power sits No. 103 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings; a win here would jump him to No. 53, unlocking a direct path through the fall playoffs

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Seamus Power is 103rd in FedEx Cup Fall standings.

A win today at Bermuda jumps him to roughly No. 53.

He's two shots off the lead going into the final round. The math is real. #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:30 AM ET

For Seamus Power, today's final round at Bermuda isn't just about a trophy or a $1.08 million check. It's about rescuing his 2026 PGA Tour season.

Power enters Sunday's round at No. 103 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. A win here would jump him to approximately No. 53 — a transformation that would open the path to the next stage of the fall playoffs and keep his PGA Tour card secure. The stakes are as real as it gets.

He has played beautifully over three rounds, co-leading at 16-under after a 67 on Saturday. His approach to the par-3 16th hole — hitting a 5-wood off the tee and a 7-iron chip into gale-force winds — showed the kind of creative, committed golf that gets players over the line in challenging conditions.

Power has won here before. He won the Bermuda Championship back in 2022. If there's one player in this field who understands how to close on this island, it's him.

article.headline: Power's FedEx Cup Stakes: Why Sunday in Bermuda Could Transform His 2026 Season

stories.title: Stifel Charity Classic Final Round — Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs Begin at Norwood Hills
stories.angle: The 2026 Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs open at Norwood Hills (Oct 23-25). Stewart Cink leads the Cup standings heading into the playoffs. Thomas Bjørn is the defending champion.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
The Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs are underway at Norwood Hills.

Stewart Cink enters as the season-long points leader. Thomas Bjørn is the defending champion at the Stifel Charity Classic.

Senior golf's playoff season has arrived. #PGATourChampions

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM ET

The PGA Tour Champions' 2026 postseason has arrived.

The Stifel Charity Classic at Norwood Hills Country Club in St. Louis is the first of three Charles Schwab Cup Playoff events, and the field is loaded with players who've been building toward this moment all year. Stewart Cink enters as the season-long Schwab Cup points leader — one of the best stretches of consistent performance in the history of PGA Tour Champions' senior ranks.

Thomas Bjørn is the defending champion, having won at Norwood Hills in 2025 at 12-under par. The Danish veteran has plenty of motivation to repeat.

The 72-player field will compete for a $2.3 million purse. Each hole matters. Senior golf's championship season is here.

article.headline: Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs Begin: Stifel Charity Classic Opens Senior Golf's Championship Season

stories.title: Thitikul's Dominant 2026 LPGA Campaign — BMW Ladies Championship Next in South Korea
stories.angle: Thitikul has won four times on the LPGA Tour in 2026, including the Lotte Championship in Hawaii; BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea is next

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Jeeno Thitikul has won four times on the LPGA Tour in 2026.

Honda Thailand. Portland Classic. Lotte Championship. She's been the dominant player of the LPGA season.

BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea is next.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:30 PM ET

The 2026 LPGA Tour season will be remembered as Jeeno Thitikul's year.

The Thai superstar has won four times in 2026, capping the most dominant stretch of her already impressive career. Her four victories include the Honda LPGA Thailand — a win in her home country — and the Lotte Championship in Hawaii, where she pulled away by three shots over Ina Yoon to claim the $450,000 winner's share from a $3 million purse.

For Thitikul, who continues to mix elite ball-striking with one of the game's most competitive on-course mindsets, the 2026 campaign has been the fullest expression of her talent to date.

Next up is the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea. The LPGA Tour's Asian swing continues, and Thitikul — playing before fans in the region who know and adore her game — will be among the overwhelming favorites.

article.headline: Jeeno Thitikul Is the LPGA's Best Player in 2026 — and the BMW Ladies Championship Is Next
